_about: Self-correction guidance for tools/code_shape.py findings, keyed by rule. Shipped only for rules that fired. Thresholds follow Ousterhout's A Philosophy of Software Design: review triggers, not orders to split.
function-lines: Over 60 lines is a prompt to look, not an order to split. Ousterhout: depth is more important than length. Extract only a self-contained subtask whose caller does not need to know how it works. Never create conjoined helpers that must be read together or that pass state back and forth. If the function reads well as one unit, raise its ceiling on the def line: `# sensors: function-lines=N -- <why it reads as one unit>`. Raising is the exception.
complexity: Too many paths to hold in your head. First try to define special cases out of existence: defaults instead of None checks, normalize input once at the boundary, a lookup table instead of an if/elif chain. Raise the ceiling only as a last resort, with a reason.
params: More than 5 parameters usually means values that travel together (make a dataclass) or pass-through variables (move the decision into the callee). Typer command functions are the exception: their parameters are the CLI surface, so ceiling them with that reason.
statements: Over 40 statements: the function probably mixes levels of abstraction. Look for a run of steps that forms one named, self-contained operation.
nesting: Deeper than 4: use guard clauses and early continue/return, or extract the innermost loop body into a function that returns a value.
file-lines: A file over 400 lines is fine if it is one deep module. Check cohesion: does everything here hide the same design decision? If yes, add `# sensors: file-lines=N -- <the decision it hides>`. If not, split by design decision, not by size.
ceiling-stale: The code improved. Lower or delete the ceiling exactly as the message says, so the ratchet keeps holding.
suppression-reason: Every `# noqa`, `# pyright: ignore`, `# type: ignore` and `# sensors:` needs ` -- <reason>` so the exception is visible and reviewable.
sensors-directive: Malformed ceiling. Syntax: `# sensors: key=INT[, key=INT] -- reason` on the def line (function keys) or on its own comment line (`file-lines`).
